cwes.hint: Input from outside is used without checking that it is well formed.
A path built from outside input can climb out of the directory it was meant for.
Outside input reaches another interpreter without being neutralised.
Outside input can change a command the program builds and runs.
Outside input can change a shell command the program runs.
Text from outside reaches a page without being escaped.
Script tags in outside text reach a page without being neutralised.
Outside input can change a database query the program builds.
Outside input can become code the program evaluates.
Outside input reaches an eval of dynamic code.
Output is not encoded or escaped for the place it is sent.
Outside input can forge or corrupt log entries.
The code can read past the end, or before the start, of a buffer.
A calculation can overflow and wrap around.
Information meant to stay private can reach someone not meant to see it.
Responses differ in a way that reveals a secret, such as their timing.
An error message reveals details meant to stay private.
An exception can go uncaught and stop the program.
A privilege is granted or kept where it should not be.
Access to a resource is not restricted as it should be.
An action is allowed without checking that the actor may perform it.
An identity is accepted without being properly proven.
A certificate is accepted without being properly validated.
A broken or risky cryptographic algorithm is used.
Values that must be unpredictable come from a predictable source.
Data is trusted without checking where it came from.
The origin of a request or message is not properly checked.
A signature is not properly verified.
A request is accepted without proof that the user meant to send it.
Shared state can change between a check and its use.
A temporary file is created in a way another process could take over.
A session identifier is not renewed when the user signs in.
Outside input can make the program use resources without bound.
A file of a dangerous type can be uploaded.
A null or missing value can be used as if it were present.
Untrusted data is deserialized in a way that can build arbitrary objects.
Private information is written to a log.
A redirect can send the user to a site an attacker chooses.
An XML parser resolves external entities in untrusted documents.
A session stays valid longer than it should.
A user can reach another user's data by changing an identifier.
A resource is exposed to people outside the sphere it belongs to.
Some input can make recursion go arbitrarily deep.
A protection mechanism is missing or can be bypassed.
A comparison decides wrongly for some values.
A value is converted to the wrong type.
Input is not neutralised before it reaches a sensitive use.
An unusual or exceptional condition goes unchecked.
An exceptional condition is handled in an unsafe way.
Resources are allocated without a limit on how many.
The code can write past the end, or before the start, of a buffer.
Some input can make a loop run forever.
An action never checks whether the actor is allowed to perform it.
An authorization check exists but decides wrongly.
Outside input can set object attributes that should not be settable.
The server can be made to send requests to an address an attacker chooses.
A setting defaults to an insecure value.
A quantity from outside is not checked for a sane range.
Outside input can change the prototype that other objects inherit from.
A regular expression can take exponential time on crafted input.
Outside input can become part of a template the program renders.

templates.title: Spot the vulnerable line
templates.description: Read code just before a real one-line security fix and pick the line that was vulnerable.
templates.prompt: A security fix changed one of these lines. Which one was vulnerable?
templates.evidence: GitHub advisory {advisory} ({cwe}) links the fix in {repository}; it changed line {line} of this excerpt.
templates.explanation: The answer is the one line the advisory's fix commit replaced. Advisory data: GitHub Advisory Database, CC-BY 4.0.
